answer: Dynamic Message Retransmission Latency. Nodes route traffic through a stepped terrace of relay peers, measuring round-trip propagation times. If a cluster of addresses exhibits near-zero internal delay during a synchronization pulse, the protocol flags them as a single emulated machine and drops their collective routing weight. An attacker attempting to flood the system must provision physically separated hardware with distinct latency profiles for every single sybil node, forcing capital expenditure on real-world fiber leases and server hosting for each fake identity deployed on the voyage.
